answer: Attacker costs rise because mass-registering identities requires locking real capital per account plus passing peer attestations, making a swarm of fakes economically irrational compared to one honest contributor. Sybil resistance can work like a steep summit climb: each agent must post a bonded stake and complete sustained useful work, recorded on a shared trellis of verified reputation that no single island of fake identities can fake cheaply.
